items.q: By the end of next year the offshore wind farm ______ power to the island for a full decade.
items.vi: Đến cuối năm sau, trang trại điện gió ngoài khơi sẽ cung cấp điện cho hòn đảo được tròn một thập kỷ.
items.explanation:
By the end of next year (a future deadline) + for a full decade (a duration) = an action continuing up to a future point, so the future perfect continuous will have been supplying is needed.
✗ will supply — simple future, cannot carry a duration up to a deadline; ✗ has supplied — present perfect measures up to now, not up to next year; ✗ will be supplying — an action in progress at that moment, not how long it will have lasted.

items.q: The novelist's leukaemia went into ______ after a year of treatment, giving her time to finish the final volume of the trilogy.
items.vi: Bệnh bạch cầu của nữ tiểu thuyết gia đã thuyên giảm sau một năm điều trị, cho bà thời gian hoàn thành tập cuối của bộ ba tác phẩm.
items.explanation:
Went into ______ after a year of treatment and giving her time show the disease eased, so the medical term remission (a period when a disease stops or improves) fits.
✗ relapse — the return of an illness after improvement, the opposite meaning; ✗ recession — a decline in the economy, not in a disease; ✗ regression — going back to an earlier, less developed state; not the word for an illness easing.

items.q: The regulator ______ badly when it approved the gas pipeline without commissioning a single environmental survey.
items.vi: Cơ quan quản lý đã sai sót nghiêm trọng khi phê duyệt đường ống dẫn khí mà không hề yêu cầu một cuộc khảo sát môi trường nào.
items.explanation:
The regulator failed in its duty (approved … without commissioning a single survey), and badly marks a mistake, so dropped the ball = failed to do what it was responsible for.
✗ kept the ball rolling — kept an activity going, a positive act; ✗ was on the ball — was alert and competent, the opposite; ✗ played ball — cooperated with someone, no sense of failure.

items.q: The city council has finally ______ approval for a second bridge across the estuary.
items.vi: Hội đồng thành phố cuối cùng đã cấp phép xây cây cầu thứ hai bắc qua cửa sông.
items.explanation:
The verb that collocates with the noun approval (also permission, a licence, a request) is grant: authorities grant approval for something.
✗ allowed — takes the thing permitted (allow a bridge / allow them to build), not the noun approval; ✗ permitted — same pattern as allow, permit + object or to-infinitive; ✗ admitted — means confess or let in, no sense of giving permission.

items.q: The switch to rooftop solar has ______ a sharp fall in electricity bills for rural households.
items.vi: Việc chuyển sang điện mặt trời áp mái đã tạo ra sự sụt giảm mạnh trong hóa đơn tiền điện của các hộ gia đình nông thôn.
items.explanation:
The switch caused a fall in bills: bring about = cause something to happen, and its object is a result (a sharp fall).
✗ brought up — raise a topic or a child; ✗ brought down — reduce or topple; you bring down bills, not a fall in bills; ✗ brought off — succeed in doing something difficult; the object is a feat, not a result.

items.q: The blackout ______ have been caused by the storm, since the transmission lines went down two hours before it reached the coast.
items.vi: Vụ mất điện không thể do cơn bão gây ra, vì các đường dây truyền tải đã đổ hai tiếng trước khi bão vào đến bờ biển.
items.explanation:
The lines went down two hours before the storm arrived, so the storm was NOT the cause: the negative past deduction can't have been (= it is impossible that it was) is needed.
✗ must — must have been says it certainly was the cause; ✗ might — might have been leaves the storm possible; ✗ should — should have been means it ought to have been, an expectation, not a deduction.

items.q: A persistent cough is often the first ______ of the lung disease that miners in the coalfield develop.
items.vi: Ho dai dẳng thường là triệu chứng đầu tiên của căn bệnh phổi mà các thợ mỏ ở vùng than mắc phải.
items.explanation:
The cough is a sign the patient notices first, so symptom = a sign of illness felt by the patient.
✗ syndrome — a whole group of symptoms that together form a condition, not one cough; ✗ diagnosis — the doctor's identification of the disease; ✗ prognosis — the forecast of how the disease will develop.

items.q: ______ must a reporter reveal the identity of a confidential source, even when the police demand it.
items.vi: Trong bất kỳ trường hợp nào, phóng viên cũng không được tiết lộ danh tính của nguồn tin bí mật, ngay cả khi cảnh sát yêu cầu.
items.explanation:
The inverted order must a reporter reveal shows a negative adverbial opens the sentence: On no account (= never, for no reason) is the only negative option and means revealing is forbidden.
✗ In any case — means anyway, not negative, so normal word order; ✗ At all costs — means whatever happens, would say the reporter must reveal; ✗ Under any circumstances — needs no (under no circumstances) to be negative and invert.

items.q: Having inflated the magazine's circulation figures for years, the publisher finally had to ______ and answer for the fraud in court.
items.vi: Sau nhiều năm thổi phồng số lượng phát hành của tạp chí, nhà xuất bản cuối cùng phải chịu trách nhiệm và trả lời về vụ gian lận trước tòa.
items.explanation:
The publisher had to accept the consequences (answer for the fraud in court), so face the music = accept punishment or criticism for what you did.
✗ call the tune — be the one in control; ✗ change his tune — change your opinion or attitude; ✗ blow his own trumpet — boast about yourself.

items.q: Unless the state broadcaster gets its ______ together, advertisers will simply take their money ______.
items.vi: Nếu đài truyền hình nhà nước không chấn chỉnh lại cách làm việc, các nhà quảng cáo sẽ đơn giản mang tiền đi nơi khác.
items.explanation:
Get your act together = organise yourself and start working properly, and unhappy customers take their money elsewhere (= to another business).
✗ show / away — the idiom is get the show on the road; take money away = remove it; ✗ house / out — the idiom is get your house in order; take money out = a withdrawal; ✗ game / off — get your game together is not an idiom; take money off = deduct.

items.q: The engineer ______ the tidal barrage was designed died before its first turbine ever turned.
items.vi: Người kỹ sư đã thiết kế đập thủy triều ấy qua đời trước khi tua-bin đầu tiên của nó quay.
items.explanation:
The barrage was designed — a passive — so the engineer is the agent and needs by: by whom the tidal barrage was designed.
✗ who — leaves the passive with no agent preposition (the engineer who the barrage was designed ✗); ✗ whom — an object pronoun but still no preposition, same problem; ✗ whose — possessive, must be followed by a noun (whose barrage), not by the article the.

items.q: The newspaper's health desk was the first to report an ______ of cholera in the flooded villages below the dam.
items.vi: Ban y tế của tờ báo là nơi đầu tiên đưa tin về một đợt bùng phát dịch tả ở các làng bị ngập bên dưới con đập.
items.explanation:
The sudden start of a disease (also war or violence) is an outbreak: an outbreak of cholera.
✗ outburst — a sudden show of emotion (an outburst of anger); ✗ outcome — the result of an event; ✗ outset — the beginning of an activity, used in at/from the outset, not with of cholera.

items.q: The national grid struggles to meet ______ demand on the hottest afternoons of the year, when every air conditioner is running.
items.vi: Lưới điện quốc gia chật vật đáp ứng nhu cầu cao điểm vào những buổi chiều nóng nhất trong năm, khi mọi máy điều hòa đều chạy.
items.explanation:
The highest level of use is peak demand — a fixed collocation like peak hours, peak season; the clue is the hottest afternoons … every air conditioner is running.
✗ top — position or rank (top speed, top floor), not a level of demand; ✗ summit — the top of a mountain or a leaders' meeting, does not modify demand; ✗ climax — the most exciting point of a story or event.

items.q: The station keeps a diesel generator on standby lest the wind farm ______ to deliver on a calm day.
items.vi: Nhà máy luôn để sẵn một máy phát diesel đề phòng trường hợp trang trại điện gió không phát được điện vào ngày lặng gió.
items.explanation:
After lest (= for fear that) the verb takes the present subjunctive: the base form fail with no -s, whatever the subject (lest the wind farm fail; should fail is the other accepted form).
✗ fails — present indicative with -s, not allowed after lest; ✗ failed — past tense, but the sentence is present (keeps) and lest never takes a past form; ✗ would fail — conditional, not used after lest.

items.q: For three years the engineers' warnings that the spillway was cracking ______, until the flood of 2019 proved them right.
items.vi: Suốt ba năm, những cảnh báo của các kỹ sư rằng đập tràn đang nứt đều bị bỏ ngoài tai, cho đến khi trận lũ năm 2019 chứng minh họ đúng.
items.explanation:
The subject is the engineers' warnings (a thing, not a person) and they were ignored, so fell on deaf ears = were not listened to.
✗ turned a deaf ear — a person turns a deaf ear to advice; the ignorer is the subject; ✗ were all ears — listened eagerly, the opposite meaning; ✗ played it by ear — improvised without a plan, needs a person as subject.

items.q: The editorial ______ an independent inquiry into the grid failure, arguing that the ministry could not investigate itself.
items.vi: Bài xã luận kêu gọi một cuộc điều tra độc lập về sự cố lưới điện, lập luận rằng bộ không thể tự điều tra chính mình.
items.explanation:
The editorial publicly demanded an inquiry, so call for = demand that something be done; the clue is arguing that the ministry could not investigate itself.
✗ called off — cancelled; an editorial cannot cancel an inquiry; ✗ called up — telephoned or summoned for military service; ✗ called out — criticised someone publicly or shouted; you call out a person, not an inquiry.

items.q: The scan revealed a ______ tumour, so the poet cancelled his reading tour to begin chemotherapy at once.
items.vi: Kết quả chụp cho thấy một khối u ác tính, nên nhà thơ hủy chuyến lưu diễn đọc thơ để bắt đầu hóa trị ngay lập tức.
items.explanation:
A cancerous tumour needing chemotherapy at once is malignant (opposite: benign), the medical term.
✗ malicious — intending to hurt (malicious gossip), describes people or actions; ✗ malevolent — wishing evil on others, a person's character; ✗ malign — as an adjective means harmful in influence (a malign effect), not a medical word for a tumour.

items.q: The pipeline was completed on schedule; ______, it ended up costing nearly twice the original estimate.
items.vi: Đường ống được hoàn thành đúng tiến độ; tuy nhiên, chi phí cuối cùng gần gấp đôi dự toán ban đầu.
items.explanation:
The gap sits between a semicolon and a comma (schedule; ______, it), a slot only a linking adverb can fill: however = but, a contrast.
✗ whereas — a conjunction, must join two clauses directly (X, whereas Y), cannot follow a semicolon; ✗ although — also a conjunction, introduces a clause with no comma straight after it; ✗ despite — a preposition, needs a noun or -ing (despite the schedule), not a clause.

items.q: ______ entirely from recycled glass, the installation changes colour as the sun moves across the gallery.
items.vi: Được làm hoàn toàn từ thủy tinh tái chế, tác phẩm sắp đặt đổi màu khi mặt trời di chuyển ngang phòng trưng bày.
items.explanation:
The installation is made from glass — it does not make anything — so the reduced relative clause is passive and needs the past participle Made.
✗ Making — active present participle, would mean the installation makes something; ✗ Having made — active perfect participle, same wrong meaning plus an earlier completed action; ✗ To make — infinitive of purpose (in order to make), not a description.

items.q: Residents ______ to stop the coal-fired plant being built on the edge of the wetland, and in the end they won.
items.vi: Người dân đã đấu tranh quyết liệt để ngăn nhà máy nhiệt điện than được xây ở rìa vùng đất ngập nước, và cuối cùng họ đã thắng.
items.explanation:
The residents struggled fiercely against the plant and in the end they won, so fought tooth and nail = fought with every possible effort.
✗ fought shy — fight shy of = avoid something, the opposite; ✗ fought like cat and dog — two people who quarrel constantly, not a campaign; ✗ picked a fight — deliberately started a quarrel, and does not take to stop.

items.q: The new arts centre ______ for audiences ______ tastes range from opera to hip-hop.
items.vi: Trung tâm nghệ thuật mới phục vụ những khán giả có gu thưởng thức trải dài từ opera đến hip-hop.
items.explanation:
Cater for = provide what a particular group wants, and the possessive relative whose links audiences to their tastes.
✗ calls / who — call for means demand, and who cannot be followed directly by the noun tastes; ✗ provides / which — provide for means support financially, and which is for things, not possession; ✗ serves / whom — serve takes a direct object with no for, and whom is an object pronoun, not possessive.

items.q: ______ the emergency generators, the newsroom would have gone dark in the middle of the election broadcast.
items.vi: Nếu không nhờ các máy phát điện dự phòng, phòng tin đã chìm trong bóng tối ngay giữa buổi phát sóng bầu cử.
items.explanation:
The result would have gone dark is past unreal (third conditional), so the condition must be past too: the inverted Had it not been for = if the generators had not existed.
✗ If it hadn't been — right tense but missing the essential for before the noun; ✗ Were it not for — present/future unreal (second conditional), mismatches would have gone; ✗ Unless there were — present unreal, and unless does not pair with a would-have result.

items.q: The condition is ______, passed from parent to child through a faulty gene, rather than caught from anyone the patient has met.
items.vi: Căn bệnh này mang tính di truyền, truyền từ cha mẹ sang con qua một gen lỗi, chứ không phải lây từ bất kỳ ai bệnh nhân từng gặp.
items.explanation:
The clue passed from parent to child through a faulty gene defines hereditary = inherited genetically.
✗ contagious — spread by contact with a sick person, ruled out by rather than caught from anyone; ✗ infectious — spread by germs from person to person, same problem; ✗ congenital — present from birth but not necessarily inherited (it can arise in the womb), so it misses the gene clue.

items.q: The volcanologist says she will never ______ the lava fountain burst through the crater floor on her first field trip to Iceland.
items.vi: Nhà nghiên cứu núi lửa nói rằng cô sẽ không bao giờ quên cảnh cột dung nham phun trào qua đáy miệng núi lửa trong chuyến thực địa đầu tiên ở Iceland.
items.explanation:
Forget + -ing = lose the memory of something that already happened; the eruption was on her first field trip, a past event, so forget seeing.
✗ forget to see — forget + to-infinitive = fail to do something you should do, not a memory; ✗ forget to have seen — the perfect infinitive is not used after forget; ✗ forget being seen — passive: she would be the one seen, but she saw the lava.

items.q: Years of rotating night shifts at the refinery ______ a heavy toll on the workers' health.
items.vi: Nhiều năm làm ca đêm luân phiên ở nhà máy lọc dầu đã gây tổn hại nặng nề đến sức khỏe của công nhân.
items.explanation:
The fixed collocation for causing serious harm is take a toll on: the shifts took a heavy toll on the workers' health.
✗ paid — you pay a toll only literally, money at a toll gate; ✗ made — make does not combine with toll; ✗ had — have a toll is not an English expression.
